Recent notes

  • Is every burst timed from its flash? 2026-08-17NTOFMatchingQADAQ

    Campaign-wide sweep of the DREAM burst time reference — 281,437 beam bursts, two independent signatures of a mis-tagged gamma flash. 48 flagged; the only 4 inside matched pulses are the ones already corrected on 16 August, so no product carries a wrong time base. Two of the three bursts the brute force could not pair are explained, and 41 "n_TOF not recording" pulses turn out to have delivered no beam to the EAR2 target either.

  • The last 88 pulses, one burst at a time 2026-08-16NTOFMatchingQABrute force

    A brute-force scan of every remaining unmatched DREAM burst against every n_TOF bunch in reach — 25 of the 88 recovered (two sub-run tails at one consistent lock each; five single bursts whose DREAM flash reference was off by 1.0 or 4.4 ms, or that the join had put three pulses over), 260 more re-attributed to n_TOF-not-recording, and the rest shown to be 11–14-trigger stubs or noise clusters. 279,938 / 279,972 = 99.99 % at the 60 % bar.

  • DREAM pedestal stability — X17 at n_TOF 2026-08-15NTOFDAQPedestalsQACampaign

    Every DREAM pedestal run of the n_TOF campaign, per channel and per chip: a doubled noise floor on 23 July, chamber A's excursion, and a connector that was dead through run_79.

  • Setting up an EOS-backed CERN site 2026-08-15CERNEOSWebeosHow-to

    Five steps from nothing to https://yourname.web.cern.ch — a folder on EOS, a share with the wwweos robot, a site record in the Web Services Portal — plus the failure modes that make it look broken when your own access is fine.

  • The 2026 X17 physics run at n_TOF EAR2 — end-of-run report 2026-08-15NTOFCampaignDAQMicromegasGamma flashTracking

    What was built, what the gamma flash does to the readout, what we actually measured, and what a post-LS3 measurement would need. 28 June – 10 August 2026. Analysis preliminary.

  • Anatomy of the unmatched 2.4% 2026-08-13NTOFMatchingQAFailure modes

    Every non-matched pulse since run_79, dissected by failure mode — and the outcome: 277,681 of 277,860 matchable pulses (99.94 % at the 60 % bar) matched after the dark hours and the never-slimmed hours were recovered on 15 Aug; n_TOF missed 0.45 % of beam pulses; the dark hours were a top-8 candidate cap, not missing data.
